question: What type of chart is used to compare parts of a whole in MS-Excel?
solution:
__**Explanation:**__

Pie charts are a popular and effective type of chart used in MS-Excel to compare parts of a whole. They provide a visual representation of data, where each slice of the pie represents a proportionate part of the total dataset. This makes it easy to see how individual parts contribute to the whole.

Pie charts are particularly useful when you want to emphasize the proportion of each category in the dataset. They are most effective with small datasets where the number of categories is limited. Each slice's size in the pie chart is proportional to the quantity it represents, making it easy to see which categories are larger or smaller relative to each other.

**Creating a Pie Chart in MS-Excel:**

 
• Select your data: Ensure your data is organized in a way that Excel can understand it. Typically, you will have one column for the categories and another for the corresponding values.
 
• Insert the Pie Chart: Go to the "Insert" tab on the Excel ribbon, click on the "Pie Chart" button, and choose the desired pie chart style from the dropdown menu.
 
• Customize the Chart: After creating the pie chart, you can customize it by adding labels, changing colors, and adjusting the layout to better suit your presentation needs.

Limited to Proportional Data: They are best suited for representing proportional data and may not be effective for displaying other types of data relationships.
